MODULE 1: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### I-ON-I BLIND

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner and a ball. Two groups can play 1-on-1 on the same basket at the same time. The defender will start 'blind' to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender's back. Once they lift the ball from the defense's back, it becomes a live 1-on-1. The offense has a maximum of three dribbles to score. Only one shot is allowed. The players are responsible for rotating and resetting the activity: the next group can begin once the defense is in the 'blind' position and they see clear space. Each repetition should have a different starting location around the 3PT line.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound, blocked shot, or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating and maintaining advantage
- Exploring different types of finishes
- Attacking the basket at different angles

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Add dribbles. 🏛️
- The defense cannot jump. 🏛️
- The offense and defense must change partners after they both play offense.
- The offense can only score at the rim inside the paint.
- The offense can only score using the net.
- The offense can only score using the backboard.
- The offense can only score using their weak hand.
- The offense can only score off two feet.
- Defense starts side by side with the offensive player (smaller advantage).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Get the players organized to read the space and successfully organize themselves by communicating whose turn it is (each repetition should start within two seconds of the one before finishing).
- Remind players to get back in line without disrupting the next group by going around the side.
- Challenge players to think about why they are using particular finishes.
- Make sure players drive from different angles and locations.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you improve your initial move to create and keep the advantage?"
- "How can you prevent the defender from recovering?"
- "Are there any adjustments that need to be made with your finish?"

Load for younger players 🏛️

### 2-ON-2 CHANGING LOCATIONS

16 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets.

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner. Each basket needs one ball and several groups. One group will begin on offense anywhere outside the 3PT line with a second group of defenders matching up. Other groups will wait their turn at the baseline. The on-ball defender will start 'blind' to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender's back. The off-ball defender can start in a gap or help position depending on their match up's placement on the 3PT line. As soon as the offense lifts the ball from the defense's back, it becomes a live 2-on-2. Games go until a basket is scored, there is a defensive stop, or the ball goes out of bounds.

#### SCORING

Offensive teams will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Keeping and maintaining advantage
- Attacking the help defense
- Scoring off 2-on-1 advantages
- Stunting and recovering
- Stopping the ball

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What other positions could you explore playing from?"
- "What can the defense do to ensure the offense does not score off the first drive?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out). If they are still inside the lava after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- After a made basket, the next team waiting at the baseline must inbound it against the team that just scored. The defenders must pressure the ball (this may include aggressively attempting to double team the receiver). The offense has five seconds to complete a successful inbounds pass. Play stops if the offense is able to inbound the ball. If the defense intercepts the ball, they can score it immediately to gain additional points.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Help players explore varied spacings, ensuring they begin from different positions.
- Officiate the 'lava' load.

### I-ON-1 CREATE SPACE

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players have 10 seconds to find a partner. Groups should divide evenly amongst all the baskets available. The offense will begin with the ball anywhere outside the 3PT area or inside the mid-range. The defender pressures the offensive player within an arms' distance. The offense has a maximum of two dribbles to create space and shoot a pull-up jump shot, but they cannot enter the paint. The defender cannot steal the ball, but can distract the shooter however they want! Change roles after three repetitions. As many as three groups can play at the same time on each basket.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense can only use one hand to steal the ball or block the offense's shot.
- The defense cannot move until the offense dribbles. If the offense tricks the defense with a false start, they gain a bonus point.
- The defense is allowed to steal the ball.
- Stay for two repetitions: the offense must attempt one rim finish and one pull-up jump shot in any sequence across both repetitions.
- Defense can start at different angles (e.g. straight up, shading to a side, etc.).

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure the players organize themselves efficiently and use all the available space.
- Make sure the defense starts arm-distance away.
- Work with offense on their decisions and reading the defender's positioning.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space
- Shooting off the dribble
- Executing ball pick-ups
- Scoring in limited dribbles

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

"What could you have done differently to create space in that situation?"

### 3-ON-3 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS

20 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of three. Make sure each basket has a minimum of three teams and a maximum of six. Teams will play half-court 3-on-3 with additional teams waiting at the baseline. After a make, the team that just got scored on sprints off while a new defensive team comes on from the baseline and touches the 3PT line before matching up and defending. Simultaneously, the offense must advance the ball and touch the half-court line to initiate the next 3-on-3.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Beating initial defense and reading second and third levels of help defense
- Identifying the open player

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What is the 'lava' load teaching?"
- "Where is the space?"
- "What are ways to speed up and take advantage of your transition?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out). If they are still inside the lava after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the 'lava' load), ready to receive the ball.
- The 'lava' load applies but post-ups are allowed.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure the players keep and communicate score.
- Make sure players start from different angles and locations.
- Remind players to create advantages by transitioning quickly after a score (offense touch half-court, defense touch 3PT line).

### 2-ON-1 I MORE

16 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Quickly introduce ROB shots (Range, Open, Balance). Divide players into groups of four with one ball per group. Two offensive players will position themselves beyond the 3PT line (either corner/wing or slot/slot). One defender starts with the ball, a short closeout position away from the two offensive players. When the defense passes the ball in, the offense has a maximum of two passes to find an open shot, but they cannot move or dribble. The defender can attempt to steal the pass or block the shot. The offensive players look to shoot and score whenever they are open. The second defender waits on the side for the first 2-on-1 to complete before they rotate in. The defenders take turns playing defense for six repetitions. After six repetitions, the offense and defense switch roles. Three groups can go simultaneously at each basket (left corner and wing, slot and slot, right corner and wing).

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, start the offense at the short corner and elbow (closer in).
- The offense is allowed to drive at any time. However if the offense drives, only 1 pass is allowed.
- The offense is allowed to cut to the basket.
- Add +1 (defender) who starts in the paint and defends after the initial pass (becomes a 2-on-1+1).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Help the players with their spacings and roles (staying on offense or defense for 6 repetitions).
- Encourage defenders to find ways to disrupt the offense.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

? (Handwritten '?')

- "Was your shot a ROB shot? If not, what was missing?"
- "In what ways can the defenders disrupt the offense?"
- "Is it possible to overpass?"

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Identifying ROB shots (Range, Open, Balance)
- Scoring off 2-on-1 advantages
